stories.body: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said US outreach was a positive step but that Tehran sees no need for direct meetings until its conditions are met. He said talks with Qatari mediators had produced a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days, rather than the five-day implementation period previously discussed. Iran is seeking sanctions relief, reduced US military forces in the region, restoration of oil waivers, release of frozen funds, and recognition of specified shipping routes. Iranian officials stressed that no meeting with US representatives is planned and that the country remains prepared for all scenarios.
stories.headline: Iran considers two-day Strait of Hormuz reopening plan as US-Iran diplomacy shows a fragile opening

stories.body: The FBI said North Korea-linked TraderTraitor actors were responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion in virtual assets from Binance on October 29, describing it as the largest cryptocurrency heist on record. The agency said the group has been converting stolen assets into Ethereum and is likely to continue laundering them through decentralized-finance and instant-swap services. Binance said it had replaced 90% of the stolen assets using its insurance funds and corporate treasury, pledged to cover the rest so users do not bear losses, and expected to resume withdrawals on Sunday.
stories.headline: FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3bn Binance cryptocurrency heist

stories.body: About 320,000 people joined a third round of cost-of-living protests across France, according to the interior ministry, while organizers put the figure near half a million. Most marches were peaceful, but clashes broke out as some rallies ended: police reported 565 arrests, injuries to five security personnel, and the use of tear gas, stun grenades, and water cannon against groups accused of violence. In Germany, tens of thousands of young people joined Gen Z-led demonstrations demanding more education funding and protesting high living costs, with clashes reported in some places.
stories.headline: Cost-of-living protests sweep France and Germany, with clashes after largely peaceful mass demonstrations

stories.body: More than 5,000 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak, with more than 10,300 confirmed cases across eight of the country's 26 provinces, according to government data. The outbreak, centered in conflict-hit Ituri province, is now the country's deadliest and has spread to Kenya, Uganda, and Nigeria; France has also reported a case involving a doctor returning from DR Congo. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved treatment or vaccine, while the response has been complicated by conflict, attacks on health workers, mistrust, inadequate equipment, and funding pressures.
stories.headline: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak becomes its deadliest, with more than 5,000 deaths reported

stories.body: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the Alliance for the Future at a Montreal summit, presenting it as a deeper Canada-EU partnership open to other countries. They said it would pursue greater economic, technological, defense, educational, and travel integration in response to climate pressures, democratic erosion, and the weaponization of trade. Canada also agreed to contribute to a €90 billion support loan for Ukraine, while the partners announced Canadian access to Europe's supercomputing network and highlighted plans to reduce reliance on US technology providers.
stories.headline: Canada and the European Union announce a new alliance open to other like-minded countries

stories.body: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk defended a contested effort by government-backed judges to take procedural control of the constitutional court, saying it was necessary to restore a tribunal he says was undermined by years of Law and Justice party influence. The confrontation followed the suspension of the court's PiS-appointed president and deputy, street protests, and President Karol Nawrocki's intervention at the building. Nawrocki has accused Tusk of a constitutional coup, while the European Commission urged him to swear in judges nominated by parliament so the court can operate in line with Poland's constitution and EU law.
stories.headline: Poland's constitutional-court dispute intensifies amid protests and competing rule-of-law claims

stories.body: A federal judge in California ordered the Justice Department and other federal officials to stop threatening state and local election workers with criminal charges or demanding that they set aside ballots based on allegations that voters may be non-citizens. The order followed federal demands involving about 20,000 California ballots, visits by armed Homeland Security officials, and reported criminal-investigation subpoenas. The ruling came days before the November 3 midterms, amid broader concerns about federal efforts to influence state-run election administration and voting rights.
stories.headline: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening election officials before midterms

stories.body: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro is campaigning for a decisive reelection victory over Trump-backed candidate Stacy Garrity while trying to help Democrats flip congressional and state Senate seats. A strong result could give Democrats control of Pennsylvania's state government for the first time since 1992 and strengthen Shapiro's standing among possible 2028 presidential contenders. Shapiro has emphasized wages, democratic institutions, and his ability to deliver results in a pivotal swing state, while declining to discuss a future presidential campaign.
stories.headline: Josh Shapiro seeks a Pennsylvania rout with possible 2028 presidential implications

stories.body: Transport Minister Óscar Puente is preparing a broad safety plan for Spain's high-speed rail network following the Urda crash, with the government expected to consider it on Tuesday. The head of the train drivers' union SEMAF said workers no longer fully trust the system and called for independent investigation, stronger operating protocols, more maintenance investment, and a limit of 40 kilometers per hour when safety systems fail. Renfe has issued an instruction bringing that speed restriction into effect, while drivers argue that increased traffic has not been matched by adequate maintenance or infrastructure investment.
stories.headline: Spain prepares high-speed rail safety plan as train drivers say confidence in the system has broken down after Urda

stories.body: The deaths of 69 people in the Urda rail disaster have intensified calls for Transport Minister Óscar Puente to resign or be dismissed, less than a month before Spain's general election. Puente has retained Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's backing and says he will remain if he is useful to the government, but faces a difficult parliamentary session on Tuesday. The opposition People's Party has paused and recalibrated its campaign, seeking to foreground management, rigor, and experience while the disaster reshapes the political contest.
stories.headline: Urda rail disaster raises pressure on Spain's transport minister and reshapes election campaign

stories.body: More than 3,500 people marched largely in silence through Valencia on the second anniversary of the 2024 DANA floods, which killed 234 people in the province. Relatives of victims and more than 200 social and union groups called for truth, justice, reparations, and political accountability over the regional government's handling of the disaster. Demonstrators criticized former regional president Carlos Mazón and the Valencian government, while the march passed without the disturbances that had prompted extensive precautionary security measures.
stories.headline: Thousands march in Valencia on second anniversary of deadly DANA floods, demanding accountability

stories.body: A large Mossos d'Esquadra and Barcelona city police operation prevented a renewed outbreak of violence linked to Blocus calls in central Barcelona, one week after looting and vandalism. More than 300 officers, including plainclothes police, conducted transport checks and preventive searches, while businesses boarded up windows or closed early. Police said they identified 1,440 people, detained three people during the operation, and filed 127 reports involving potentially dangerous items or drugs; the operation also led to the arrest of a fourth person allegedly tied to earlier Blocus activity.
stories.headline: Mass police deployment prevents renewed Blocus violence in Barcelona

stories.body: A court in Torrent, Valencia, ordered the alleged founder and main promoter of Blocus in Spain held without bail while investigators examine accusations that he created and administered Telegram groups used to encourage public disorder, shop break-ins, and property damage. The court also barred him from accessing computers and internet-connected devices. Another suspect was also remanded without bail in the Valencian Community, and police across Spain have made multiple arrests connected to Blocus channels and alleged efforts to organize looting and violence.
stories.headline: Alleged Blocus founder remanded in custody without bail as investigations continue

stories.body: Catalan police arrested a 21-year-old man in Cabrera d'Anoia as a fourth suspect in Catalunya connected to Blocus communication channels accused of promoting the October 24 looting and violence in Barcelona. Police say he administered a group promoted through a TikTok poster and WhatsApp link, actively helped energize it, and was in Barcelona during the disturbances. The arrest follows detentions of two minors and an 18-year-old, as investigations continue into organizers and participants across Spain.
stories.headline: Catalan police make fourth arrest linked to Blocus channels accused of organizing Barcelona looting

stories.body: Spain's government has revised a proposed decree regulating data centers and would give the competition regulator, CNMC, authority to review compliance with environmental, electricity, security, and data-sovereignty requirements every six months. The draft maintains a requirement that facilities ultimately secure 80% renewable electricity on an hourly basis, but gives them five years to meet it under transitional conditions. Technology companies have strongly opposed the proposal, arguing that some obligations are unworkable and considering legal challenges, while the government hopes to approve the rules before the November 29 election.
stories.headline: Spanish government gives competition regulator authority to oversee data centers' environmental and security obligations
